label: CONVICTION EARNED
call: The council would sell about a third of the Costco position and keep the rest, because one stock at a quarter of the portfolio [F015] is more risk than the business itself.

why.point: It has fallen 53% before [F014]. At a quarter of the portfolio, a repeat would hurt far more than the business deserves.
At 55 times earnings [F009] against a 10-year average of 36, much of the next few years' return has already arrived.
Keeping two thirds keeps you in a business where nine in ten members renew every year.

minority.quote: You do not sell a wonderful business because it went up.
minority.would_have_to_be_true: Buffett would be proven right if growth at existing stores stays above 6% and the price keeps rising with earnings.

premortem: Costco keeps compounding and the third you sold was the best part of your portfolio.
You sell the third, then sell the rest in a panic during a fall.
The money from the sale sits idle or goes into something worse.

kill_criteria.text: Growth at stores open a year or more falls below 4%
The price climbs further above its usual level

conditions: Sell in steps over a few weeks
Keep the rest unless a kill criterion trips
cheapest_test: Sell the first tenth this week and see how it feels.
sizing_note: Ask what share of everything you own you could watch halve and still sleep.

behavioral_flags.quote: I want to lock in the gain

lean_pull_note: Selling it all gained 0.4 after the lean was shared; it still ranks last.
data_health: Prices, filings, rates and news ok; no analyst estimates.

seat_lines.buffett: Never sell a wonderful business only because it went up.
seat_lines.munger: Trim for sanity, keep the core.
seat_lines.marks: Trimming is managing risk, not forecasting.
seat_lines.taleb: Size so a halving is survivable.
